decision.detail: I swing my legs over the side of the mattress. Feet hit carpet. Cold. I stand. I don't look at the window. I don't listen to the radio finish its three notes. I pull my shirt over my head, step into the pants that are still in the chair, tie the tie one-handed the way I've done it four hundred mornings. Coat. Gloves in the left pocket. The small paper with the address in the right. I walk down the corridor. I don't stop at the lobby. I don't look at Rita or Larry or the ballroom lights or the piano or the Rialto or the flat tire or the envelope on the coat-check rack. I walk to the coach that's pulling up outside, I put my hand on the back of a seat to steady myself, and I sit. The bus drives. Pittsburgh is two hours. I will be there by seven. I will be at her door at seven-fifteen with the gloves and the coffee money in my pocket. The couch is a couch. It is in Pittsburgh. I am going to Pittsburgh. That is the whole forecast. Nothing else is in the forecast.
decision.intention: Be on that bus. Be in Pittsburgh by seven. Be at her door at seven-fifteen. The couch is a couch. She is counting on me. I go.
decision.words: One word, to the bus driver, as I sit down: "Pittsburgh."
